The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Najruddin, aged about 47 years, suffered fatal injury resulting in his death.

The claim for compensation is being pursued by Smt. Bhuri (aged about 46 years), as dependent widow wife of deceased and her children Nazreen (daughter, aged about 23 years), Najis (daughter, aged about 22 years), Mohd. Azeem (son, aged about 19 years), Vajis (son, aged about 14 years), Mohammad Nadeem (son, aged about 8 years),
Saniya MACT No.532/2021 Bhuri & ors. vs. Bhure @ Mohd. Bhura & ors. Page no. 2 of 9 ss (daughter, aged about 13 years) and Sajiya (daughter, aged about 8 years).
2.

Brief facts of the case are that on 27.03.2021 at about 11:00 a.m. when victim Najruddin along with one Mehfooz, s/o Chhote, was standing along the Road side, a motorcycle bearing no.UP-21BK-8817 (hereinafter referred as to the offending vehicle) came all of a sudden from behind.
It was being driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the victim.
Driver of the offending vehicle fled from the spot towards Sirsi.
Due to the impact, victim sustained grievous injury.
Ambulance was called and victim was removed to Sambal Hospital where he was referred to Siddh Hospital, Moradabad, U.P.
Victim died during treatment on 04.04.2021.
Postmortem was conducted and matter was reported to the police.
3. An FIR no.0267/2021, dated 13.06.2021 u/s 279/304A of IPC was registered at PS Sambhal.
Police investigated the matter and filed a chargesheet u/s 279/304-A of IPC before concerned Criminal court while the present claim petition filed before this Tribunal.

4. As per record, the offending vehicle was driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured with respondent no.3.
5.

Respondent no.1 and 2 filed their written statement denying their liability to compensate on the ground that the offending vehicle was insured at the time of accident with respondent no.3/ IFFCO Tokio General Insurance company vide policy no.MH727255 valid from 10.01.2021 to 09.01.2022.

Negligence of the driver has also been denied pleading that the MACT No.532/2021 Bhuri & ors. vs.

sentences.text: Whether this Tribunal has territorial jurisdiction to deal and try with the present petition?

OPP. 
10.
In the present case, jurisdiction of this Tribunal has been claimed on the basis of location of one of the branch offices of respondent no.3 within the territorial jurisdiction of this Tribunal.
As per law settled in Malti Sardar vs. NIC, there is no bar to a claim petition being filed at a place where the insurance company, which is the main contesting party, has its business.
Thus, the plea of lack of Territorial Jurisdiction is unsustainable and issue is accordingly decided.

Issue No.2 Whether the deceased died in a road traffic accident on 27.03.2021 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no.UP-21BK-8817 being driven by R-1/Bhure and owned by Dilshad/R-2 and insured with R3?OPP. \

11. Before proceeding to decide the above issue, it is apposite to note that as a settled principle of law, proceedings under The Motor Vehicle Act are not considered akin to the proceedings in a civil suit and hence strict rules of evidence are not applicable.
Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors.

12. In the present case, petitioners have examined Mehfooz/PW2 as eye witness, to prove the occurrence of the accident and rash and negligence of the offending vehicle.

On the other hand,
respondent no.3 has refuted the claim on the ground that there is a delay of 78 days in lodging of the FIR.
It is pleaded that the offending vehicle has been planted and that PW2 is only an interested witness who has not witnessed the accident.

The testimony of PW2 reveals that though he claims to have witnessed the accident alleging that he was standing along with the deceased by the road side, it has nowhere been cited or pleaded as to where exactly the accident took place.

Further, PW2 has admitted that though he was carrying a Bhuri vs Bhure @Bhoora on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135725839/
4 mobile phone at the time of accident, he never attempted call either the police or the ambulance after the accident.
He further admitted that he did not inform the family members of the deceased about the accident despite being a resident of the same village as that of the deceased.
He has conceded that even the alleged driver of the offending vehicle is also a resident of the same village.
He has stated that he had informed one Tahir, who was a neighbour of the deceased, about the accident but did not inform the police.
Also, while claiming to have remained present at the spot till the victim was taken in an ambulance to Sambhal Hospital, PW2 conceded that he did not even accompany the victim to the hospital.
During cross examination PW2 admitted that he did not see the offending vehicle since he was facing the other side.

He MACT No.532/2021 Bhuri & ors. vs.

sentences.text: Page no. 7 of 9 ss pleaded ignorance as to the speed of motorcycle which hit the victim or as to who was riding the same prior to the accident.

The version of PW2 thus fails to inspire confidence as it is highly improbable that if the accident was witnessed by PW2, who also happens to be a resident of the same village, he would not have called the police or the ambulance or atleast informed the family of the victim about the accident.
It has further not been explained by PW2 that how, despite facing the other side, he noted the number of the offending vehicle or identified its driver.
Petitioners have also not produced any Tahir, whom PW2 claims to have informed about the accident.
On the contrary wife of the deceased/PW1 Bhuri alleged to have got information about the accident from PW2 and one Usman.
PW1 has admitted that PW2 was known to her being from the same village.
PW-1 has also admitted that neither PW2 nor Usman nor her brother in law Kamruddin inform the police or file any complaint soon after the accident.
Further, the chargesheet also does not cite PW-2 Mehfooz or Tahir or Usman as eye witnesses to the accident.

In such circumstances, a delay of 78 days in registration of FIR from the date of accident and 70 days delay from date of death of the victim without any call or compliant to the police renders the claim of occurrence of the accident due to involvement of the vehicle, itself doubtful.
In fact even the GD entry as to accident was made only after 9 days from the accident, after death of the victim.

Further, even the mechanical inspection report does not reveal any damage to the front side of the offending vehicle from where it is claimed to have hit the victim nor there is any MACT No.532/2021 Bhuri & ors. vs. Bhure @ Mohd. Bhura & ors.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Page no. 8 of 9 ss evidence if the offending vehicle was repaired soon before its inspection.

Thus the inordinate delay in reporting the incident or disclosing the details of the offending vehicle or its driver despite him being a resident of the same village as that of the victim and the alleged eye witness and no supporting material to show death due to accident involving any vehicle, raises strong doubt as to the veracity of the claim.

In view of the above discussion, it is held that the petitioners have failed to prove occurrence of the accident due to involvement of any vehicle much less the offending vehicle, even by preponderance of probabilities.
As such, issue no.2 is decided against the petitioners and in favour of the respondents.

14. Present claim petition is accordingly dismissed.
